newsitem.title: MEXICO: Modelo Q2 earnings bubble on beer exports.
newsitem.headline: Modelo Q2 earnings bubble on beer exports.

text.p: Capitalizing on a seemingly unquenchable thirst abroad for its flagship Corona brand, Mexican brewer Grupo Modelo SA turned in positive second quarter results boosted by export sales, analysts said.

Modelo said its exports for the second quarter of the year were 1.56 million hectolitres (41.2 U.S. gallons), an increase of 48.9 percent in volume terms from the same period in 1996. Analysts had previously predicted an increase of 25-30 percent.
The company posted total sales of 3.924 billion pesos between April and June -- well above the 3.514 billion pesos forecast by analysts in a previously conducted Reuters survey.
Net earnings meanwhile came to 504 million pesos, up from a year-ago figure of 417 million pesos and a total of 437 million pesos predicted by analysts.
"Export growth was unbelievably good," said Gregory Rianhard, an analyst at Mexico City's Interacciones brokerage.
For Julio Zetina of Caspian Research, domestic sales volumes growth was also encouraging and "outstripped expectations."
Modelo sold a total of 7.9 million hectolitres (208.6 million U.S. gallons) of beer during the second quarter, or 13.4 percent more than year-ago figures.
Analysts said the gain showed consumers had recovered from a beer price rise in March.
Marco Vera of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said "the second quarter is traditionally strong for Modelo," due to warmer weather and thirstier consumers.
Analysts said the main disappointment in Modelo's report was sales costs, which rose to 1.945 billion pesos for April-June from 1.515 billion pesos for the same period last year.
Modelo said in a statement the increase was due to greater export volumes.
